prototype_feel_reasons: The lower locked hotspot is placed directly over the cement mixer drum, obscuring the object players need to recognize and judge.
The crane lock overlaps functional crane machinery, weakening the subject-first hierarchy.
On mobile, the intentionally wide scene cuts off substantial right-side content without a strong visible affordance that the image itself is horizontally scrollable.
The desktop composition leaves a very large empty lower area, making the finished screen feel vertically unfinished despite the polished scene frame.
Hotspot treatments vary between an hourglass icon, translucent locks, and a large speech label, producing inconsistent visual weight across one scene.
issues: port scene/lower locked hotspot — translucent lock badge covers the cement mixer drum, an important job object — move the badge into adjacent pavement or place it above the vehicle with a short connector.
port scene/crane locked hotspot — badge sits over the crane mechanism and partially masks its readable structure — reposition into nearby open sky and connect it to the crane.

mobile/scene viewport — right-side truck and dock content are cut off at the initial position while the swipe instruction is visually weak — add a clearer edge fade, partial continuation cue, or initial horizontal position that preserves the primary subjects.

desktop/screen composition — framed scene and instructions occupy only the upper half, leaving excessive blank space below — tighten the page height, vertically center the content group, or use the remaining space for progression/navigation.
port scene/hotspot system — icon, lock, and speech-bubble presentations have uneven scale and prominence — standardize hotspot badge size, opacity, border treatment, and label anchoring.
BADGE_COLLISION: overlay covers a subject's face/head/tools
